title: Monitors
description: Composable health checks with dependencies: every check runs on its own schedule; links explain failures (root causes) and keep follow-up alerts quiet.

templates.intro: A template is a monitor with parameters (IP address, asset id, cadence …). Create many monitors from it with a form or a CSV file; when the template changes, instances show "template updated" and can be re-synced.
templates.none: No templates yet. Import "{{example}}" from the example library.

gateways.intro: A gateway (for example the plant's IoT gateway) reports many heartbeat checks in one call to <c>{{endpoint}}</c>, mapped by the check key. It has one secret; the allowed keys limit what it may report.
gateways.rotateConfirm: Rotate the secret of "{{name}}"? The current secret stops working immediately.
gateways.deleteConfirm: Delete gateway "{{name}}"? Its reports will be rejected.
gateways.copyNowText: It is shown only once. Store it in the gateway's configuration; rotate it if it may have leaked.
gateways.manyInOneCall: Report many checks in one call
gateways.reportFormat: Each report: key (the check key), ts (ISO 8601 or Unix time, optional), value, status (up/degraded/down, optional) and data. HMAC mode: add X-Steward-Gateway with the gateway id and X-Steward-Signature.
gateways.allowedCheckKeysHint: Wildcard *, e.g. m17.* – required: a gateway may only report the keys listed here, and only for monitors its owner may edit

secrets.title: Heartbeat secrets
secrets.copyNowText: Each secret is shown only once and cannot be recovered. Store it in the reporting system (for example the IoT gateway). If one is lost or leaked, rotate it on the check.

form.name: Name
form.allowedDelayHintCadence: How much later than its timestamp the data may arrive (gateway upload cycle, ingestion): missed intervals are counted from the age minus this. Default 0.
form.allowedDelayHintMaxAge: How much later than its timestamp the data may arrive (gateway upload cycle, ingestion): down only when older than the maximum age plus this. Default 0.
form.checkIdHint: Letters, digits, _ and -; used in links, item keys and the API
form.fallbackPortHint: Used when ICMP is not available (default 80)
form.useProxy: Use the proxy from the environment
form.variablesHint: The newest value of each must be fresh; the worst counts
form.sharedCall: Checks on the same asset and aspect share one Insights Hub call per cycle.
form.timestampHint: Over the response body; a timestamp or a list (the newest counts)
form.statusExpressionHint: Returns up, degraded, down or true/false; default: the report's status field
form.gatusMaxAge: Down when the newest result is older than (s)
form.gatusRecent: Degraded on failures in the last N results
form.subMonitorHint: Evaluated on its own schedule; this node shows its aggregated status
form.critical: Critical (a failure takes the monitor down)
form.gatusSourceHint: Metrics: the state Steward scrapes from Gatus' /metrics (Platform → Metrics). API: Gatus' status API (needs basic auth when Gatus is protected).

gatusSources.auto: Automatic (metrics when enabled for the platform)

form.cmkServiceHint: The service description exactly as in CheckMk, e.g. "Filesystem /var". Empty: the state of the host
form.cmkMaxAgeHint: Optional: the state counts as unknown when CheckMk has not checked it for this long
form.promQueryHint: An instant query, e.g. 100 * (1 - node_filesystem_avail_bytes{mountpoint="/var"} / node_filesystem_size_bytes{mountpoint="/var"}). With several series the worst one counts
form.promNoDataHint: Usually unknown: the target may have disappeared
form.k8sDeploymentHint: Empty: every deployment of the namespace
form.gitAlertsHint: GitHub Dependabot; empty: alerts are not checked
form.kafkaWithinHint: Empty: new messages are not checked
form.kafkaSchemaHint: Of <topic>-value in the Schema Registry; empty: not checked
form.connectConnectorHint: Empty: every connector of the cluster
form.connectNotRunningAs: When a connector or task failed
form.connectPausedAs: When one is paused or stopped
form.connectFailedMinutesHint: Empty: at once; before that, degraded
form.connectMaxLagHint: Read on the Kafka platform of the cluster; empty: not checked
form.connectQuietHint: No message on any topic of a Debezium connector; empty: not checked
form.confluentConnectorHint: Its name or id (lcc-…); empty: every managed connector of the organisation
form.confluentClusterHint: Its id (lkc-…) or name; empty: every Kafka cluster of the organisation
form.mqttTopicHint: + one level, # the rest, e.g. plant/+/status
form.mqttModeAny: A message on any matching topic
form.mqttModeEach: A message on every topic seen (silent devices)

snowflakeObjectHint.tasks: DATABASE or DATABASE.SCHEMA – from ACCOUNT_USAGE, up to 45 minutes behind
snowflakeObjectHint.credits: The warehouse name – from ACCOUNT_USAGE, up to 3 hours behind

form.snowflakeFailAs: When the limit is not met
form.dtrackProjectHint: name@version, name@latest or the project's UUID in Dependency-Track
form.dtrackMaxHighHint: Degraded above; empty: high findings are not checked
form.dtrackPolicyFail: A failing policy violation counts like a critical finding
form.lastReportHint: {{when}} – the condition and status expression see exactly these fields
form.lastReportNone: No report received yet (or the check is not saved yet). Once the gateway reports, its last report is shown here.

entraModes.app-credentials: App secrets and certificates that expire

form.entraWithinDaysHint: Per app registration and type, the secret or certificate that lasts longest counts: a rotated one next to a newer one does not.
form.entraDownWithinDays: Down when expiring within (days, expired too)
form.entraAppsHint: Display names or application ids; empty: every app registration
form.entraServicesHint: e.g. Exchange Online, Microsoft Teams; empty: every service. Needs ServiceHealth.Read.All.
form.vaultFolderHint: Only secrets of this folder and below, e.g. \IT\Servers; empty: every secret the service account may list
form.vaultPrivilegedFoldersHint: Secrets in these folders (and below) count as privileged: they need checkout and approval, and any finding on them fails the check. Enter a path and press Enter.
form.vaultPrivilegedTemplatesHint: Secrets of these templates count as privileged too, e.g. Windows Account

dbModeHints.connection: Connects and signs in; degraded when the account can write
dbModeHints.replication: The largest replication lag in seconds (replicas of a primary, or this standby)
dbModeHints.query: The first column of the first row of a read-only query, compared with WARN and CRIT

form.dbParamsHint: One value per placeholder, in order (Enter adds one)

dbNoDataHints.replication: When the server has no replica and is no standby
dbNoDataHints.query: When the query returns no row

form.headersHint: Sent with the request; the platform's own authentication is added as usual.
form.requestBodyHint: JSON, or text sent as it is. Only with POST – for APIs that read with POST (search, GraphQL, JSON protocols).

ddbModeHints.newestItem: One Query per partition key value: Limit 1, newest first by the sort key – the time attribute is usually the sort key. Only the key and the time attribute are read.
ddbModeHints.writeActivity: ConsumedWriteCapacityUnits of the table: the newest minute with writes is the age. CloudWatch is a few minutes behind – allow at least 10 minutes.
ddbModeHints.hygiene: Status ACTIVE, point-in-time recovery and time to live. Item count and size are values for trends (AWS updates them about every six hours).

form.ddbIndexHint: A secondary index whose sort key is the time; empty: the table's own key
form.ddbPartitionValuesHint: Each with its own age, e.g. device#press-07 (at most 20; press Enter after each)
form.ddbFailAs: When a requirement is not met
form.ddbPolicy: Read-only: needs dynamodb:Query and the Describe actions on the table (and its indexes), cloudwatch:GetMetricData for the write activity – see docs/AWS.md.
form.dbSchemaSystemHint: A system of the service catalogue whose tbls schema is pushed to Steward

dbSchemaModeHints.breaking: A removed table or column, a narrowed type, NOT NULL without a default, a removed key
dbSchemaModeHints.changed: Any added, removed or changed table, column, key or index

form.dbSchemaReadHint: Reads the schema at every check (a snapshot when it changed). Off: only the reads and imports already stored count.
form.versionApplicationHint: Its components and the systems it runs on are checked against the newest versions the version watch knows
form.versionEnvironmentHint: Only this environment (and what serves all); empty: every one
form.versionProductsHint: Only these; empty: the whole tech stack
form.versionMaxDays: Degraded when behind for more than … days
form.versionMaxDaysHint: Since the first newer release; empty: not checked
form.versionEolAs: Release cycle at its end of life
form.pageWatchWatchHint: As Steward last read them from changedetection.io
form.pageWatchUuidHint: The UUID of the watch in changedetection.io (in the address of its edit page: /edit/<UUID>)
form.pageWatchNotRead: Steward has not read the watches of this platform yet: read them on its Watches tab to pick one, or enter the UUID.
form.pageWatchTagHint: The name of the tag in changedetection.io; case does not matter
form.pageWatchFailingAsHint: Its last check failed (fetch error, filter not found) or it was not checked in time
form.pageWatchMaxCheckAgeHint: Counts as failing; empty: not looked at
form.pageWatchChangedAsHint: Information: the check stays OK and names the change

periods.month: The last month with the month before
periods.monthToDate: This month so far with the same share of the month before

cost.currencyHint: Empty: the one with the highest costs

form.contractHint: The check runs with the monitor owner's rights: they must see the contract (and, for tests, may test it and use its service and database)
form.noContract: No data contract you may see

contractModeHints.test: Runs the contract's test; the full report is stored with the contract
contractModeHints.findings: No owner, not tested recently, last test failed, columns that no longer match – without the service

form.contractTestHint: A test reads data: it gets at least a minute, whatever the time limit above says (at most 300 s). A test run of the monitor (recorded responses) does not call the service – it judges the last stored run.

detail.deleteConfirm: Delete "{{name}}" with its history? Heartbeat URLs stop working.
detail.templateUpdatedText: This monitor was created from an older version of its template. Re-sync replaces the definition with the current template version (parameters stay).
detail.disabled: This monitor is paused – its checks do not run and it sends no messages. Resume it at the top of the page.
detail.graphHint: Arrows point from a check to the checks that depend on it. Dashed: soft link (both run; a failing parent explains the child). Solid: hard link (the child is not evaluated while the parent is down). Click a check for details.
detail.likelyCausedByNoAlert: Likely caused by {{causes}} – no separate alert is sent for this check.
detail.openHiddenMonitor: Includes a monitor you cannot view.
detail.pauseConfirm: A paused monitor runs no checks and sends no messages until it is resumed; its status shows as unknown, also to monitors that depend on it. For planned work use a maintenance window instead: the checks keep running and only the messages pause.

maintenance.intro: Checks keep running and their results are recorded, but the monitor shows "maintenance", notifications and runbooks are silenced, and the time does not count against uptime.
maintenance.vsPause: To stop the checks altogether, pause the monitor at the top of the page.
maintenance.catalogue: Maintenance windows are planned under Maintenance; a window can list the monitor itself or reach it through a platform it checks.
maintenance.reachesMonitor: Reaches this monitor through a platform

outputs.title: Outputs

notification.label: Notification (in-app, e-mail, Teams)
notification.help: The owner and the subscribers are notified about root causes only; dependent failures are folded into one alert.

webhook.label: Webhook (JSON)
webhook.help: POSTs { source, monitor, events[] } with status, status code, root causes and the latest message.

gatus.label: Gatus external endpoint
gatus.help: Pushes success/error to POST /api/v1/endpoints/<key>/external with the platform credential "externalToken".

zabbix.label: Zabbix
zabbix.help: sender: trapper protocol to port 10051 (items of type Zabbix trapper); api: history.push (Zabbix 7.0+, API token). Values: 0 up, 1 degraded, 2 down, 3 unknown, 4 blocked, 5 maintenance.

process.label: Start a process (runbook)
process.help: Starts the runbook as the monitor owner; inputs are JSONata over { monitor, check, event }.

outputs.intro: Outputs send status changes (and optionally every evaluation) to people and other monitoring systems. Placeholders in keys and paths: {{placeholders}}.
outputs.none: No outputs yet – the status is still available in the API, Prometheus metrics and dashboards.
outputs.holdHint: Wait this long so a parent failing a little later still explains the failure (default 0)
outputs.urlHint: Without credentials; for authenticated targets choose a platform instead
outputs.manageOnly: Only the owner, administrators or users with the manage right can change outputs.
outputs.runMessages: Messages of the runs it starts
outputs.formatHint: Teams card: an Adaptive Card per status change, posted to a Teams channel
outputs.teamsChannelHint: A platform of kind "Microsoft Teams channel (Workflows)": it keeps the Workflows URL encrypted, and its access list decides who may post there
outputs.urgentHint: A change to down reaches people and channels at once, also during their quiet hours (unless they turned that off).
outputs.stateChangesHint: Monitors with states: also a message for information when the state changes, e.g. Running → Off (never urgent)
outputs.whileOffHint: What Gatus gets while the monitor is off; a contradiction and Off beyond the maximum are always failures

heartbeat.rotateConfirm: Rotate the secret? The reporting system must use the new one right away.
heartbeat.setupIntro: Heartbeat checks are fed by another system, for example the IoT gateway: either one call per check with that check's secret, or one call for many checks with a gateway secret (Monitors → Gateways), mapped by the check key. A missing report turns the check down without any request. Body (JSON, max. 64 KB): status (optional: up, degraded, down or true/false), value, ts (ISO 8601 or Unix time) and data.
heartbeat.gatewayKey: Gateway key: <c>{{key}}</c> · secret {{prefix}}… (shown only when created or rotated)

editor.description: Add checks from the palette and connect them: drag from the lower handle of a check to the check that depends on it.
editor.linkHint: Soft: both checks run; when both fail, the dependent check is reported as "likely caused by" the other and no separate alert is sent. Hard: the dependent check is not evaluated (blocked) while this one is down.
editor.selectHint: Select a check to edit it, or click a link to change it.
editor.startHint: Start with a check from the palette.
editor.keyHint: Stable identifier for integrations (Zabbix item keys, LLD, Prometheus, heartbeat keys); default from the name

rules.quorum: Quorum: k of n critical checks up

editor.isTemplate: This is a template (parameters as {{example}}, edited as YAML)
editor.templateYaml: Templates are edited as YAML: {{example}} placeholders may stand anywhere, also where numbers are expected. They are replaced when monitors are created from the template.
editor.linkHowTo: Link cards by dragging from the lower edge of a card to the card that depends on it. A new check is placed below the selected card and depends on it – remove the link when it does not.
editor.previewNote: Tried as it is in the editor, not saved. Nothing is recorded.
editor.selectionHint: Duplicate them together: the copies keep the links between the selected checks.
editor.multiSelectHint: Shift-click or drag a box with Shift held to select several checks.
editor.saveAsTemplateIntro: Creates a monitor template from the saved monitor. The fields you choose become parameters (their current values are the defaults); each new monitor from the template gets its own values.
editor.saveAsTemplateUnsaved: Unsaved changes are not part of the template – save the monitor first.
editor.templateNoFields: The checks have no fields that can become parameters.
editor.templateParamsHint: The same parameter name for several fields fills them all with one value. In the template the fields read {{example}}.
editor.templateBadParam: Parameter “{{name}}”: letters, digits and _ only, starting with a letter (not “name” or “key”).

acknowledge.title: Acknowledge – {{name}}
acknowledge.intro: Tells others that someone is working on the problem. Further notifications of this monitor are held back until it is up again.

instances.title: New monitors from "{{name}}"
instances.csvHint: One line per monitor. Columns: the parameter names, plus optional "name" and "key". Comma or semicolon separated; the first line is the header.

statusInfo.unknown: No data yet, or the check itself could not run
statusInfo.blocked: Not evaluated because a hard dependency is down
statusInfo.maintenance: In a maintenance window – alerts are silenced
statusInfo.off: Off – all checks agree with an expected state (no alert)

ping.label: Ping
ping.help: ICMP echo via the system ping command; falls back to a TCP connect when ping is not available

tcp.label: TCP port
tcp.help: Opens a TCP connection to host:port

http.label: HTTP(S)
http.help: Calls a URL: expected status, JSONata condition on the body, response time, TLS certificate expiry

platform.label: Platform API
platform.help: Calls an operation through a configured platform (its authentication, base URL and retries)

freshness.label: Data freshness
freshness.help: Latest timestamp of a data source must be recent: expected cadence or maximum age (Insights Hub time series preset)

heartbeat.label: Heartbeat (push)
heartbeat.help: Another system (e.g. an IoT gateway) reports to Steward; missing reports turn the check down

gatus.label: Gatus endpoint
gatus.help: Status of an endpoint monitored by Gatus

checkmk.label: CheckMk host or service
checkmk.help: Current state of a host or service in CheckMk (OK, WARN, CRIT, UNKNOWN)

prometheus.label: Prometheus query
prometheus.help: A PromQL query compared with WARN and CRIT levels; with several series the worst one counts

kubernetes.label: Kubernetes deployments
kubernetes.help: Deployments of a namespace are ready (e.g. 3/3) and no pod is crash-looping

git.label: Repository pipeline
git.help: The pipeline of the default branch on GitHub, GitLab or Forgejo passes; optionally few enough open security alerts

kafka.label: Kafka topic
kafka.help: New messages on a topic within N minutes, the lag of a consumer group, a group that is stuck, the schema version

kafka-connect.label: Kafka Connect connectors
kafka-connect.help: Connectors and their tasks are RUNNING, a task failed for N minutes, the consumer lag of a sink connector, a Debezium connector whose topics got no message for N minutes

confluent.label: Confluent Cloud
confluent.help: The Kafka clusters of a Confluent Cloud organisation are provisioned, or its managed connectors and their tasks are RUNNING (a task failed for N minutes)

mqtt.label: MQTT topics
mqtt.help: Messages on an MQTT topic within N minutes, devices (topics of a pattern) that went silent, connected clients

monitor.label: Sub-monitor
monitor.help: The aggregated status of another monitor (evaluated on its own schedule)

snowflake.label: Snowflake
snowflake.help: A Snowflake table changed recently enough, no task of a database failed, or a warehouse stayed within its credits

database.label: Database
database.help: A database platform: the connection works (and is read-only), replication lag stays below a limit, or the value of a read-only query is judged against WARN and CRIT levels

db-schema.label: Database schema changes
db-schema.help: The schema snapshots of a database platform or a system: no change, or no breaking change, within the last N hours; optionally reads the platform first

dependency-track.label: Vulnerabilities (Dependency-Track)
dependency-track.help: A Dependency-Track project has no more open critical (or high) findings than allowed and no failing policy violation

version-behind.label: Version behind
version-behind.help: The tech stack of an application is up to date: degraded when more minor releases or days behind than allowed, down when a major release behind or the release cycle reached its end of life (version watch)

entra.label: Entra ID (Microsoft Graph)
entra.help: App registrations whose secrets or certificates expire within N days, or the Microsoft 365 service health

privilege-vault.label: Vault hygiene (IBM Verify Privilege Vault)
privilege-vault.help: Secrets of IBM Verify Privilege Vault: failed heartbeats, passwords not rotated or expired, automatic changing off, no owner, privileged secrets without checkout or approval

dynamodb.label: DynamoDB table
dynamodb.help: A DynamoDB table on an AWS platform: the newest item per partition key is recent enough, the table had writes within the window (CloudWatch), or its status, point-in-time recovery and time to live

page-watch.label: Page watch (changedetection.io)
page-watch.help: Watches of changedetection.io: a page changed within the last N hours (informational or degraded), a watch whose last check failed or that was not checked for too long

cost.label: Cost change
cost.help: The costs of a service, application, team or platform: up by more than a percentage or an amount compared with the month before

data-contract.label: Data contract
data-contract.help: An ODCS data contract: its test through the data contract service passes (warnings degrade), or Steward’s own checks – owner, last test, columns of linked datasets and tables – find nothing

emptyState.title: No monitors yet
emptyState.text: Monitors you may see will show up here.
emptyState.textCreate: Watch devices, APIs and data flows with composable checks. Create a monitor, or import an example from the library.

platformChoices.title: Platforms
platformChoices.label: Platform for “{{ref}}”
platformChoices.noneOfKind: You may use no platform of kind {{kind}}. Add one, or ask for the “use” right on one.
platformChoices.noneOfKinds: You may use no platform of the kinds {{kinds}}. Add one, or ask for the “use” right on one.
platformChoices.none: You may use no platform. Add one, or ask for the “use” right on one.

testRun.title: Test run with recorded responses
testRun.help: The platform checks answered by the recorded responses of their platforms. Nothing is stored: no results, no status change, no messages. Other check types need the network and are skipped.

observed.title: Peak age before new data ({{days}} days)
observed.figures_one: median {{median}}, 95 % {{p95}}, max {{max}} · delay {{delay}} · {{count}} sample · checked every {{every}}
observed.figures_other: median {{median}}, 95 % {{p95}}, max {{max}} · delay {{delay}} · {{count}} samples · checked every {{every}}
observed.none: No sample yet: one is taken when a read sees a newer value than the read before (checked every {{every}}).
observed.worstVariable: Figures and suggestion of the variable that gets oldest: {{name}}
observed.notEnough_one: A suggestion needs {{hours}} hours and {{samples}} samples – so far {{coverage}} and {{count}} sample.
observed.notEnough_other: A suggestion needs {{hours}} hours and {{samples}} samples – so far {{coverage}} and {{count}} samples.
observed.note: Upper bounds: a figure can be up to one check interval too high, so use a short interval while measuring. Differences of the device clock are part of the figures (only a clock that is ahead can be detected).
observed.suggestion: Suggested from the 95 % peak age of {{p95}}, rounded up to the minute, plus one check interval ({{margin}}):
observed.covered: The current settings already cover the observed peak age.

states.offTime: Off as expected 24 h {{h24}} · 7 d {{d7}} · 30 d {{d30}} (not counted)
states.changesLastHour_one: {{count}} state change in the last hour
states.changesLastHour_other: {{count}} state changes in the last hour
states.intro: States tell when the checks are expected to fail: a machine switched off on purpose is grey and quiet (Off), and only checks that contradict the state raise an alert. The first row whose condition matches wins; Otherwise evaluates the monitor as without states.
states.followsHint: A monitor that cannot tell its state itself: its rows name the other monitor’s state ids
states.maxOffHint: Off for longer is degraded and notifies; empty: {{hours}} h, 0: no maximum
states.leaderIds: States of the monitor it follows: {{ids}}
states.name: Name of state {{n}}
states.tryHint: Set each check to a status: which state wins and what the monitor would report (nothing is stored; settle times are left out).
states.otherwiseWins: No state matches – evaluated as without states
states.caption: Decision table: one row per state, one column per check
states.legendSelects: the condition: the first row whose condition matches wins.
states.legendExpected: what the check is while the state holds; a check that deviates after the settle time is a contradiction.
states.legendRequired: Required: the check must be up for the state to be trusted, otherwise the monitor is down at once.
states.legendOff: Off is offered only in sub-monitor columns (a sub-monitor that is off itself); a check of its own is Down when its device is off. Whether a state shows grey Off is the Shows column.
states.legendContradiction: what a contradiction in this state makes the monitor: Down (default) or Degraded. The other way, per check: a check without “Critical” (in its card) only degrades the monitor when it deviates.
